findings.description: `publish()` sets `s.posted` to the full proof count and saves it before patching the PR description or posting proof comments. If a `gh` call fails or the process stops between those operations, `continueRun()` sees the saved count and returns early, leaving the missing description or comments unpublished.
findings.title: Proofs marked posted before they land

citations.citation: Require GitHub evidence before persisting runner completion markers

**7. The runner trusts what GitHub shows, not its own notes** (the Fresh Read Rule)
- **Rule:** the runner decides from what GitHub shows now, all of it: every page of comments, events and labels, read with `allPages`. What it saves between runs (counts, markers like `lastAsk` and `pushedAt`, local files like `<n>-pr-body.md`) is only a note. When a note and GitHub disagree, GitHub wins. Nothing is marked posted, read or done until GitHub shows it happened.
- **Where:** `scripts/agent-watch.mjs` and `scripts/runner-lib.mjs`: every read of tickets, PRs, comments, events and labels, and everything the runner saves about them. Rule 3 covers the same idea in `web/`.
- **Why:** this was the most common cause in Qodo's reviews of the runner: 8 of its 26 findings, across 4 PRs. I wrote the rule from #48, #51 and #53, then checked it against #60, which it hadn't seen. It predicted 3 of #60's 6 findings. The rest belong to other causes.
- **Breaks it:** reading only the first 100 comments or events (#48). Changing the local PR description and not the PR (#51). Moving `lastAsk` past an instruction that hasn't been carried out (#53). Saving a proof as posted when it was only rehearsed (#60).
- **Checked by:** `tests/runner-lib.test.mjs` (`allPages` reads past 100, `publishPlan` works out what to post from the PR itself, `askPlan` marks a comment read). In review: any GitHub read that stops at one page, any decision made from a saved note that GitHub could contradict and anything marked done before GitHub shows it.

evidence.explanation: In `publish()`, `s.posted = s.proofs.length; save(n, s);` runs before the description PATCH and `comment(s.pr, p)` calls, so the completion marker can advance without GitHub confirming those writes. The saved count is checked before further writes, and both the post-push and recovery paths use this publication flow; the existing planner and tests cover partially completed publication.

findings.description: `publish()` treats an absent `s.posted` as zero and posts every proof after the first without checking existing comments. State files saved by the previous runner have no such field, so the next tick on an existing multi-proof PR repeats comments that were already published.
findings.title: Existing pull requests get duplicate proofs

citations.citation: A previous count-based publisher reposted comments already present on older pull requests.

evidence.explanation: The new line is the only writer of `posted`; existing state loads without migration, and the old remote planner explicitly avoids reposting comments found on the PR. The same legacy-state duplication was previously fixed in PR #60.

findings.description: `publish()` uses the saved `s.posted` count instead of checking the live PR body and owner's comments before deciding that all proofs are present. If a proof is removed from the description, a comment is deleted, or a comment fails to post while the count remains complete, later runner steps and `/agent` retries do not restore the missing proof.
findings.title: Publishing skips the PR's real state

citations.citation: Reconcile runner decisions against current GitHub state rather than saved notes

evidence.explanation: The `if (done >= s.proofs.length) return` check exits before any remote reconciliation, and `publish()` no longer calls `ghJson(...pulls...)` or `issueComments(...)` to read the PR body and comments. The existing `publishPlan` identifies missing proofs from that remote content, while the runner's documented source-of-truth rule says GitHub wins when saved markers disagree with it.
